verses.note: The church fathers often read "Let Us" as a first glimpse of the Trinity. Most interpreters today agree the first readers would not have heard it that way, but many still think it fitting that the fuller revelation of Father, Son, and Spirit makes sense of the plural. The verse does not prove the doctrine; the doctrine rests on the New Testament.

The Trinitarian reading of verse 24 has an ancient history in Christian interpretation, but most modern commentators, Christian and Jewish, see a Hebrew stylistic repetition. The doctrine of the Trinity rests on the New Testament, not on this verse.
